long_biography.plain_text:
Alex Haagen III has spent much of his working life reshaping Southern California shopping centres. In the company his father established, he negotiated development projects while still in his twenties and later oversaw design, construction and property management. He served as vice-chairman of the family's publicly traded property trust before the family sold its interest in 1997.

Haagen continued the work through the privately held Haagen Company, where he is chairman and chief executive. Its projects range from neighbourhood retail centres to the redevelopment of existing malls. He also developed the Empire Polo Club in Indio, adapting land bought for polo into a venue for major music festivals and other events.

proposed_details.existing_value:
Formerly known as Hideout, the Princess Y85 luxury yacht, named Empire Sun, was delivered in 2021. In October 2022, the yacht was put up for sale by Boomer Jousma from The Italian Yacht Group, with a listed price of $7,250,000.

Evidence suggests that the yacht underwent a change of ownership around May 2023, leading to a modification in its name. According to records from the Federal Communications Commission (FCC), Empire Sun is presently registered under the ownership of Alex Haagen III, hailing from Los Angeles, California.

Alex Haagen III holds the position of Chairman and CEO at Haagen Company, an esteemed Real Estate Investment firm managing assets exceeding $700 million. The company specializes in procuring, developing, and overseeing retail shopping centers as well as commercial properties.

Beyond his real estate enterprises, Mr. Haagen III is the proprietor of the Empire Polo Club situated in Indio, California. This renowned venue is renowned for hosting major events such as the Coachella Music Festival and the Stagecoach Country Music Festival, drawing large crowds of music enthusiasts every year.
